\"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// 3D index calculation\ninline constexpr size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// Compute Laplacian with clamped boundary conditions\ninline double computeLaplacian(const double* c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                               const double dx, const double dy, const double dz, const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z) {\n    const size_t xp = (x < nx - 1) ? x + 1 : x;\n    const size_t yp = (y < ny - 1) ? y + 1 : y;\n    const size_t zp = (z < nz - 1) ? z + 1 : z;\n    const size_t xn = (x > 0) ? x - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t yn = (y > 0) ? y - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t zn = (z > 0) ? z - 1 : 0;\n    \n    const double cxx = (c[idx3(xp, y, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(xn, y, z, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dx * dx);\n    const double cyy = (c[idx3(x, yp, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, yn, z, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dy * dy);\n    const double czz = (c[idx3(x, y, zp, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, y, zn, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dz * dz);\n    \n    return cxx + cyy + czz;\n}\n\n// Compute chemical potential\nvoid computeChemicalPotential(const double* c, double* mu,\n                              const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                              const double dx, const double dy, const double dz,\n                              const double gamma, const double e_AA, const double e_BB, const double e_AB) {\n    // Parallelize over the (z, y) plane; static schedule keeps the same\n    // thread->memory mapping in every sweep (first-touch NUMA locality).\n    #pragma omp parallel for collapse(2) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                const double cv = c[idx];\n                \n                mu[idx] = 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * e_BB - 2.0 * cv * e_AB) \n                         + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n                         - gamma * computeLaplacian(c, nx, ny, nz, dx, dy, dz, x, y, z);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Cahn-Hilliard update step\nvoid cahnHilliardUpdate(double* cnew, const double* cold,\n                        const double* mu,\n                        const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                        const double D, const double dt, const double dx, const double dy, const double dz) {\n    #pragma omp parallel for collapse(2) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                cnew[idx] = cold[idx] + dt * D * \n                           computeLaplacian(mu, nx, ny, nz, dx, dy, dz, x, y, z);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Initialize concentration field\nvoid initializeConcentration(double* c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    const size_t vol = nx * ny * nz;\n    \n    #pragma omp parallel for collapse(2) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                // Generate pseudo-random value in [-1, 1]\n                const size_t linear_id = z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n                const double pseudo = ((((linear_id + 1) * 1299709) % vol) / static_cast<double>(vol));\n                c[idx] = -1.0 + 2.0 * pseudo;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const double* c, const size_t n) {\n    // Check for NaN or Inf\n    bool nonFinite = false;\n    #pragma omp parallel for reduction(|:nonFinite) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        nonFinite |= !std::isfinite(c[i]);\n    }\n    if (nonFinite) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    if (n == 0) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    \n    // Check if values are in reasonable range for concentration field\n    // After Cahn-Hilliard evolution, values should typically remain bounded\n    double minVal = c[0];\n    double maxVal = c[0];\n    #pragma omp parallel for reduction(min:minVal) reduction(max:maxVal) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        minVal = std::min(minVal, c[i]);\n        maxVal = std::max(maxVal, c[i]);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Concentration range: [%.6f, %.6f]\\n\", minVal, maxVal);\n    \n    // Values should generally stay within reasonable bounds\n    if (maxVal > 10.0 || minVal < -10.0) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: values out of expected range\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -x <num>     Grid size in X dimension (default: 64)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -y <num>     Grid size in Y dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -z <num>     Grid size in Z dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of time steps (default: 20)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t nx = 64;\n    size_t ny = 0;\n    size_t nz = 0;\n    int iterations = 20;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-x\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nx = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-y\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            ny = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-z\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nz = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    if (ny == 0) ny = nx;\n    if (nz == 0) nz = nx;\n    \n    printf(\"Cahn-Hilliard Phase Separation Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Grid size: %zu x %zu x %zu\\n\", nx, ny, nz);\n    printf(\"Time steps: %d\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Physical parameters\n    const double dx = 1.0;\n    const double dy = 1.0;\n    const double dz = 1.0;\n    const double dt = 0.01;\n    const double e_AA = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_BB = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_AB = (2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double gamma = 0.5;\n    const double D = 1.0;\n    \n    const size_t gridSize = nx * ny * nz;\n    \n    // Allocate arrays without zero-filling them on the main thread; they are\n    // first written inside the parallel loops so pages are placed NUMA-locally.\n    auto cold = std::make_unique_for_overwrite<double[]>(gridSize);\n    auto cnew = std::make_unique_for_overwrite<double[]>(gridSize);\n    auto mu = std::make_unique_for_overwrite<double[]>(gridSize);\n    \n    // Initialize concentration field\n    printf(\"Initializing concentration field...\\n\");\n    initializeConcentration(cold.get(), nx, ny, nz);\n    \n    // Run simulation\n    printf(\"Running Cahn-Hilliard simulation...\\n\");\n    auto start = That's odd, and I'm not sure static scheduling with one thread explains it.\n\nI wonder if libgomp adds overhead even with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, or if there's a spin-wait happening that shouldn't exist for a single-thread parallel region. The rows version also hits 68 despite only incurring one division per row call, so that overhead doesn't explain the gap either. I'm now considering whether it's really memory bandwidth or first-touch effects given the three 128MB arrays, but since initialization happens identically in both versions, that doesn't seem to account for the difference—so I'm looking more closely at how the z-loop executes in the outlined version.\n\nSince none of these theories are panning out, I should just try `perf stat` directly to see where the time is actually going rather than continuing to speculate, and check whether the slowdown is really in compute versus some initialization phase that might be getting measured.\n\n","time":{"start":1792950898824,"end":1792950905426},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1792950985574,"sessionID":"ses_e8bcfcc7affellkQ5Di8f7tOe2","part":{"id":"prt_17434ba38001DpVy9ZKHKjeiqr","messageID":"msg_17434b65e0013L055YVtIJ1rtT","sessionID":"ses_e8bcfcc7affellkQ5Di8f7tOe2","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm looking at why this kernel is division-bound with three vdivsd ops per cell, and wondering if the serial version had dx constant-propagated since dx=1.0 was likely a literal in main, letting the compiler simplify the division away.\n\nThe real issue is that the outlined function receives dx2 at runtime through a struct, forcing actual divisions instead of the compile-time elimination the inlined serial version got. Replacing division with multiplication by a reciprocal wouldn't preserve bit-exact results unless dx2 is a power of two, so the fix has to preserve the division while restoring the inlining/constant-propagation path, likely by keeping dx, dy, dz as compile-time constants that propagate into the OpenMP version the same way they did in main.\n\nMaking the physical parameters constexpr at namespace scope lets the compiler fold them without reassociation, preserving bit-exact results since no fast-math is involved. I'd define constants like dx, dy, dz, dt, and the energy terms directly, removing the need to pass them as function parameters.\n\nI'll just remove the dx/dy/dz params entirely and rely on the global constexpr values directly inside the kernel functions, since passing them as runtime params defeats the folding. Now I'm going to rewrite the actual file with these edits applied carefully.\n\n","time":{"start":1792950975032,"end":1792950985506},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1792950985575,"sessionID":"ses_e8bcfcc7affellkQ5Di8f7tOe2","part":{"id":"prt_17434e327001voylUaoPrkGJ32","messageID":"msg_17434b65e0013L055YVtIJ1rtT","sessionID":"ses_e8bcfcc7affellkQ5Di8f7tOe2","type":"text","text":"The profile points to the cause. In the outlined OpenMP kernel the spacings `dx`, `dy`, `dz` are runtime parameters, so each cell performs three `vdivsd` instructions. In the original serial build those parameters are the constant `1.0`, so after inlining the compiler folds the divisions away and vectorizes the loop.\n\nThe fix is to make the fixed physical constants `constexpr` at namespace scope and stop passing them as parameters. `x / 1.0` and constant products fold exactly, so the results remain bit-identical. I'll apply that to the real file.","time":{"start":1792950985511,"end":1792950985528}}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1792950998131,"sessionID":"ses_e8bcfcc7affellkQ5Di8f7tOe2","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01HGccxon1vpmhSi8wm66Pmm","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cahn-hilliard_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r1/cahn-hilliard/cahn_hilliard.cpp","content":"#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <memory>\n#include <utility>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Physical and discretization parameters. They are compile-time constants so\n// the optimizer can fold them into the (OpenMP-outlined) kernels; this removes\n// per-cell divisions by the grid spacing and keeps results bit-identical.\ninline constexpr double dx = 1.0;\ninline constexpr double dy = 1.0;\ninline constexpr double dz = 1.0;\ninline constexpr double dt = 0.01;\ninline constexpr double e_AA = -(2.0 / 9.0);\ninline constexpr double e_BB = -(2.0 / 9.0);\ninline constexpr double e_AB = (2.0 / 9.0);\ninline constexpr double gamma = 0.5;\ninline constexpr double D = 1.0;\n\n// 3D index calculation\ninline constexpr size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// Compute Laplacian with clamped boundary conditions\ninline double computeLaplacian(const double* c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                               const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z) {\n    const size_t xp = (x < nx - 1) ? x + 1 : x;\n    const size_t yp = (y < ny - 1) ? y + 1 : y;\n    const size_t zp = (z < nz - 1) ? z + 1 : z;\n    const size_t xn = (x > 0) ? x - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t yn = (y > 0) ? y - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t zn = (z > 0) ? z - 1 : 0;\n    \n    const double cxx = (c[idx3(xp, y, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(xn, y, z, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dx * dx);\n    const double cyy = (c[idx3(x, yp, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, yn, z, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dy * dy);\n    const double czz = (c[idx3(x, y, zp, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, y, zn, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dz * dz);\n    \n    return cxx + cyy + czz;\n}\n\n// Compute chemical potential\nvoid computeChemicalPotential(const double* c, double* mu,\n                              const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    // Parallelize over the (z, y) plane; static schedule keeps the same\n    // thread->memory mapping in every sweep (first-touch NUMA locality).\n    #pragma omp parallel for collapse(2) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                const double cv = c[idx];\n                \n                mu[idx] = 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * e_BB - 2.0 * cv * e_AB) \n                         + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n                         - gamma * computeLaplacian(c, nx, ny, nz, x, y, z);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Cahn-Hilliard update step\nvoid cahnHilliardUpdate(double* cnew, const double* cold, const double* mu,\n                        const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    #pragma omp parallel for collapse(2) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                cnew[idx] = cold[idx] + dt * D * \n                           computeLaplacian(mu, nx, ny, nz, x, y, z);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Initialize concentration field\nvoid initializeConcentration(double* c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    const size_t vol = nx * ny * nz;\n    \n    #pragma omp parallel for collapse(2) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t z = 0; z < nz; ++z) {\n        for (size_t y = 0; y < ny; ++y) {\n            for (size_t x = 0; x < nx; ++x) {\n                const size_t idx = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                // Generate pseudo-random value in [-1, 1]\n                const size_t linear_id = z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n                const double pseudo = ((((linear_id + 1) * 1299709) % vol) / static_cast<double>(vol));\n                c[idx] = -1.0 + 2.0 * pseudo;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const double* c, const size_t n) {\n    // Check for NaN or Inf\n    bool nonFinite = false;\n    #pragma omp parallel for reduction(|:nonFinite) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        nonFinite |= !std::isfinite(c[i]);\n    }\n    if (nonFinite) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    if (n == 0) {\n        return true;\n    }\n    \n    // Check if values are in reasonable range for concentration field\n    // After Cahn-Hilliard evolution, values should typically remain bounded\n    double minVal = c[0];\n    double maxVal = c[0];\n    #pragma omp parallel for reduction(min:minVal) reduction(max:maxVal) schedule(static)\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        minVal = std::min(minVal, c[i]);\n        maxVal = std::max(maxVal, c[i]);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Concentration range: [%.6f, %.6f]\\n\", minVal, maxVal);\n    \n    // Values should generally stay within reasonable bounds\n    if (maxVal > 10.0 || minVal < -10.0) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: values out of expected range\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -x <num>     Grid size in X dimension (default: 64)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -y <num>     Grid size in Y dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -z <num>     Grid size in Z dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of time steps (default: 20)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t nx = 64;\n    size_t ny = 0;\n    size_t nz = 0;\n    int iterations = 20;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-x\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nx = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-y\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            ny = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-z\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nz = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    if (ny == 0) ny = nx;\n    if (nz == 0) nz = nx;\n    \n    printf(\"Cahn-Hilliard Phase Separation Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Grid size: %zu x %zu x %zu\\n\", nx, ny, nz);\n    printf(\"Time steps: %d\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    const size_t gridSize = nx * ny * nz;\n    \n    // Allocate arrays without zero-filling them on the main thread; they are\n    // first written inside the parallel loops so pages are placed NUMA-locally.\n    auto cold = std::make_unique_for_overwrite<double[]>(gridSize);\n    auto cnew = std::make_unique_for_overwrite<double[]>(gridSize);\n    auto mu = std::make_unique_for_overwrite<double[]>(gridSize);\n    \n    // Initialize concentration field\n    printf(\"Initializing concentration field...\\n\");\n    initializeConcentration(cold.get(), nx, ny, nz);\n    \n    // Run simulation\n    printf(\"Running Cahn-Hilliard simulation...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    for (int t = 0; t < iterations; ++t) {\n        // Compute chemical potential\n        computeChemicalPotential(cold.get(), mu.get(), nx, ny, nz);\n        \n        // Update concentration\n        cahnHilliardUpdate(cnew.get(), cold.get(), mu.get(), nx, ny, nz);\n        \n        // Swap buffers (O(1) pointer swap)\n        std::swap(cold, cnew);\n    }\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n    \n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate performance\n    double cellUpdates = (double)gridSize * iterations;\n    double mcups = cellUpdates / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e6;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f MCellUpdates/s\\n\", mcups);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        const std::vector<double> result(cold.get(), cold.get() + gridSize);\n        print_results(result, \"Concentration\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateResult(cold.get(), gridSize);\n        \n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return 0;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cahn-hilliard_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r1/cahn-hilliard/cahn_hilliard.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cahn-hilliard_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_omp_r1/cahn-hilliard/cahn_hilliard.cpp","time":{"start":1792950998061,"end":1792950998094}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_17434ec83001T2v6m7JRdvSXno","sessionID":"ses_e8bcfcc7affellkQ5Di8f7tOe2","messageID":"msg_17434e380001LdqAEurVrCZm15"}}
